title: Logic Errors
body:
The program compiles, runs to completion, exits cleanly, and is wrong. No message, no
crash, no line number. The compiler cannot help because there is nothing wrong with the
C++; the machine did exactly what you wrote, and what you wrote is not what you meant.

[[Errors]] has the worked example: `cout << "2 + 3 ="` followed by `cout << 2 * 3`, which
prints `2 + 3 = 6`. Both lines are perfectly legal.

The usual sources:

- `=` where `==` was meant. `if (x = 0)` assigns and is always false.
- Off-by-one in a loop bound. `i <= size` instead of `i < size` walks one past the end of
  the [[Array]], and because C++ does not check bounds it usually does not crash.
- Integer division truncating. `(a + b) / 2` on ints throws away the half; see
  [[Division Algorithm]].
- Operator precedence, or the wrong operator entirely, as in the example above.
- Wrong initial value on an [[Accumulator]]: starting a sum at 1 or a product at 0.
- Passing by value when you needed [[Call by reference|reference]]. The function computes
  the right answer and then throws it away. `swap()` is the standard demonstration.

Logic errors are the expensive ones because finding them costs more than fixing them. The
only reliable defence is deciding what the answer *should* be before you run it, which is
what an [[Algorithm]] written down on paper buys you, and then testing against that with a
[[Driver]]. [[Program design]] and [[Function design]] are the up-front half; [[debugging]]
is the after-the-fact half.

They also compound with [[Runtime Errors]]: an out-of-bounds read that happens not to crash
is a logic error wearing a runtime error's clothes.

Same category exists at every level of the degree. [[Assembly Errors]] calls it a
"run-time behavioural error" in [[COMPUTING MACHINERY]], and
[[INTRODUCTION TO SOFTWARE ENGINEERING]] builds [[Unit testing]] specifically to catch it,
because it is the only one of the three that testing is genuinely required for.

The other two thirds of the taxonomy: [[Compile Errors]] stop the build, [[Runtime Errors]]
crash. See [[Errors]].
